items.review_rationale: Read the whole reduced induced closed subscheme definition. Distinguished the underlying closed subset from its scheme structure, reduction, and the uniqueness among reduced closed subschemes.

references.phrase: underlying topological space of a subscheme
references.context: Algebraic geometry: underlying topological space of a closed subscheme with inherited topology

references.disposition: Uniqueness is confined to the induced reduced closed subscheme, not all schemes with the same closed underlying set.

items.review_rationale: Read every clause of pointwise reducedness of the local rings of a scheme, distinguishing the structure-sheaf stalk from section rings and the reduced-ring condition from weaker absence of zero divisors.

references.context: Sheaf theory: stalk of the scheme structure sheaf at a point x

references.disposition: The definition requires every local ring to be reduced; a single reduced stalk is insufficient.

items.review_rationale: Examined the entire equivalent sectionwise characterization of a reduced scheme, retaining the quantifier over all open U rather than checking only global sections.

references.phrase: ring O_X(U) has no nonzero nilpotents

references.context: Sheaf theory: section ring of the scheme structure sheaf over an open subset

references.disposition: Universal quantification is over all opens, not just affines or the full space.

items.review_rationale: Reviewed the full pointwise neighborhood-refinement characterization of a basis and its containment quantifiers without countability or metrizability assumptions.

references.context: Set theory: family of subsets, here all open in X

references.phrase: some basis member contains x and lies in U
references.disposition: The defining basis condition is local refinement for every x in every open U.
